external_confirmation.correspondent: Dr. Frank Förster, University of Bonn / Egyptian Museum
external_confirmation.exact_effect: Förster reports that he contacted the authors of the 2016 volume, who confirmed that all relevant data were published there, including compositional data for QH 207/39 and QH 207/40. He explicitly states that the volume can be regarded as the frozen surviving source-bound analytical record sought by the project.

publication.title: Materialien einer Gusswerkstatt von der Qubbet el-Hawa
publication.authors: Martin Fitzenreiter, Frank Willer, Johannes Auenmüller et al.
publication.source_file: /Google Drive/JANUS Research/QH207 Qubbet el-Hawa/Materialien einer Gusswerkstatt von der Qubbet el-Hawa (Fitzenreiter-Willer-Auenmueller 2016).pdf
relevant_sections: Kap. 6 chemical composition and lead isotopes

bulk_alloy_sampling.preparation: Sample location cleaned locally to bright metal with a 1 mm diamond ball grinder to reduce corrosion contamination; drill samples with ambiguous/internal corrosion were excluded.
bulk_alloy_sampling.selection_constraint: Only accessible pieces without obvious surface corrosion were considered; some bronzes inside moulds were inaccessible.

lead_isotope.note: Two objects also had tiny surface scrapings for comparison with drilled metal samples.

qh207_40_gilding.conclusion: clear gold signal; publication identifies the layer as gold leaf; Hg absent in the reported measurement, used to exclude fire gilding.

qh207_39.mould_contents: four Osiris figures; three bronze foot/lower fragments with wax-modelled missing upper bodies plus one inverted composite/hollow-cast broken figure

published_interpretation: Pb is just under 8%, interpreted as intentional lead addition.
Lead-isotope composition differs strongly from the other Qubbet el-Hawa samples; no direct ore match is identified.
Anatolian lead ores are discussed only as a possible maximum association, with mixing/recycled lead explicitly complicating provenance.
The tin level 5.4% places QH 207/39 among the 'Altbronzen' exceptions in the assemblage.

technical_context: μCT shows repair/re-membering preparation rather than a simple new casting event.
At least one composite figure in QH 207/39 includes evidence interpreted as a workshop-fresh failed casting, so the mould cannot be treated as uniformly made from previously used cult fragments.
missing_for_discrimination: The publication does not bind MA-145253 to a named one of the four individual bronze fragments/figures.
No fragment-by-fragment elemental dataset is published for all bronze pieces inside the mould.

qh207_40.mould_contents: four Osiris figures with previously cast bronze foot/lower fragments and wax-modelled missing upper bodies

printed_table_inconsistency.handling_rule: Do not silently correct. Because Kat. 4.3 elsewhere consistently denotes QH 207/40, treat QH 204/40 as a printed internal inconsistency requiring source clarification if the surface-scrape identity becomes decisive.

gilded_foot_pXRF.caveat: The measurement area exceeds the surviving gilding; copper and mould-sand are co-measured. The table is therefore qualitative for confirming gold, not a clean quantitative gold-alloy composition.

technical_context: Three feet end just above the ankle in clear sharp breaks; a fourth preserves most of the lower body including buttocks.
The exposed lower foot region on one side bears the thin gold layer detected by HDR microscopy and p-XRF.
missing_for_discrimination: The publication does not bind MA-145254 explicitly to one of the four named/positioned bronze fragments.
Only the gold-leaf p-XRF is explicitly spatially tied to a specific exposed foot part.
No complete fragment-by-fragment chemical map is published.

cross_object_result.published_fact: QH 207/39 and QH 207/40 have substantially different bulk alloy compositions and lead-isotope signatures; the volume explicitly argues that the metal remains are heterogeneous and cannot derive from one casting batch.
cross_object_result.limits: One bulk drill-sample record per mould cannot establish the distribution of compositions among the four fragments within each mould.
cross_object_result.source_authors_interpretation: The volume states that /39 and /40 likely contain fragments of older castings or used statuettes and views the heterogeneous metals as compatible with accumulated failed/repaired castings over time.

discrimination_test_assessment.question: Is the published 2016 record sufficient to discriminate a ritual-preservation model from a purely technological/recycling/experimental model?
what_it_can_test: Whether /39 and /40 are chemically identical products of one casting batch: NO; published chemistry rejects that simple model.
Whether at least one /40 fragment had a finished pre-repair surface: YES; gold leaf on a specific foot fragment strongly supports prior finishing/use-stage completion.
Whether QH207 special forms contain mixed lifecycle material: YES when chemistry is combined with μCT/catalogue evidence.
what_it_cannot_test: Whether every bronze fragment in /39 and /40 was previously used as a cult image.
Whether reused/finished fragments are chemically distinct from workshop-fresh fragments within the same mould.
Whether chemistry itself favors ritual deposition over ordinary workshop recycling/repair, because fragment-level mapping and a matched technological control set are absent.
discrimination_test_assessment.exact_missing_datum_if_future_contact_ne: For each individual bronze fragment in QH 207/39 and QH 207/40: sample-to-fragment mapping (which foot/figure was MA-145253 and MA-145254 taken from), and whether any additional fragment-specific measurements exist. Do not ask generally for 'all unpublished compositional data' unless this specific mapping is shown to survive outside the publication.

response_debt.recommended_action: Send a brief thank-you confirming that the 2016 volume has now been treated as the frozen analytical source; do not immediately ask for more archival data.

canonical_seal: PUBLISHED 2016 ANALYTICS ARE THE CURRENT FROZEN RECORD. ONE SAMPLE PER MOULD IS NOT A FRAGMENT-LEVEL MAP.
